# Previously-failing fuzz cases — one `target seed size version` per line (`#` starts a comment,
# blanks ignored). `fuzz` appends a minimal repro here automatically when it finds a NEW failure;
# fix the bug, commit the new line, and `regressions` replays it forever. Do not hand-edit the
# numbers — the trailing comment is the only free-form part.
#
# `version` is the generator fingerprint (`v_utils::fuzz::fnv`), taken per target over the sources
# that decide what its `(seed, size)` means. A pair names a *trace* only under that generator:
# reshape it and the same pair replays some unrelated trace — a random run wearing a regression
# test's name, which is worse than no test, because it reports green for a case it never runs. So
# `regressions` replays only lines at the current version, and prints how many it skipped.
#
# NEVER DELETE A LINE. A superseded line stops being a test, but it does not stop being the record
# of what once broke and why, and that costs nothing to keep.
# A PRODUCT FINDING, reported and not fixed (a fuzzer that finds a bug in logic it does not own says
# so and keeps going). The documented bootstrap loop does not close for an adverb: `skeleton` sends
# every non-VERB to `names`, `Glossary::allows` honours a name only as NOUN/PROPN/ADJ, so the word
# returns at the next run still telling you to add what you already added. The first version of this
# target did not find it — the generator's out-of-vocabulary pool was all nouns, so the arm that
# decides where a suggested word goes was never taken. Widening that pool by three adverbs found it
# at seed 0. See the quarantine in text.rs, which fails once the design call is made.
suggest 0 5 308352503  # the suggested glossary left 1 unknown-word finding(s): ["`asynchronously` is not in the ASD-STE100 approved vocabulary. Add it to `docs/glossary.nix` if it is a Technical Name or Technical Verb."]
